Implicit Parameter Transformation

Source: R/parameters.R
Pimpl.Rd

Solves \(f(x, p) = 0\) for the states \(x\) by pseudo-transient continuation (cppDE::ptc()) and returns a parfn with sensitivities from the implicit function theorem.

Usage

Pimpl(
  trafo,
  parameters = NULL,
  forcings = NULL,
  condition = NULL,
  keepRoot = TRUE,
  flow = inherits(trafo, "eqnlist"),
  compile = FALSE,
  modelname = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  deriv = TRUE,
  deriv2 = FALSE,
  controlsPTC = list(),
  outdir = .dmodOutdir()
)

Arguments

trafo

Named character, eqnvec or eqnlist defining \(f\), in the language of cppDE::expressions.

parameters

Outer parameter names. For an eqnlist the totals \(T\) of the conserved quantities are added. States named here are held at their value instead of solved for, and a state whose right-hand side is "0" becomes a parameter.

forcings

Forcing names, set to 0. Default NULL.

condition

NULL (default) for a transformation valid in every condition, or the name of the condition it belongs to.

keepRoot

If TRUE (default), roots are kept and repeated calls with the same values are answered from memory.

flow

If TRUE, \(\dot{x} = f(x, p)\) and a stable steady state is returned. If FALSE, any regular root. Default TRUE for an eqnlist, else FALSE.

compile

Logical. TRUE compiles now, FALSE (default) leaves it to compile().

modelname

Base name of the generated files, default NULL, which is "impl_parfn", followed by _<condition>.

verbose

Logical. Print the compiler output, default FALSE.

deriv, deriv2

Build first and second derivatives, default TRUE and FALSE. deriv2 requires deriv = TRUE.

controlsPTC

Named list of solver controls; an entry not given keeps the default, an unknown entry is an error:

reltol, abstol

Convergence tolerances, default 1e-10, 1e-14.

flowTol

Relative local error per pseudo-time step, default 1.

maxit

Iterations per start, default ceiling(70 * log(n + 1)) for n states.

dtInit

Initial pseudo-time step relative to the fastest rate, default 1e-2.

positive

Keep states positive, default TRUE.

stability

Require a stable root if flow = TRUE, default TRUE; where no start reaches one, the evaluation fails. With FALSE an unstable root is returned, on which a constraintStability() term rises.

stabilityTol

With stability, a root counts as stable while the real part of the leading eigenvalue on the manifold of the conserved quantities is at most the larger of 1e-8 times the largest eigenvalue modulus there, the precision of the eigenvalues, and stabilityTol, an absolute value in the units of the rates; default 0. A positive value admits a resting state that departs from rest more slowly than a time scale of interest, as near a Hopf bifurcation. constraintStability() reaches the weight at stabilityTol.

stabilityMargin

The width of the ramp of constraintStability() below stabilityTol, relative to the largest eigenvalue modulus on the manifold of the conserved quantities; default 1e-6.

nStarts

Random starts after the deterministic ones, default 20.

startRange

Range of a random start, drawn uniformly per state on startScale, default c(-5, 5).

startScale

"log10" or "linear", default "log10" if positive and "linear" otherwise.

seed

Seed of the random starts, default 1. The starts depend on the seed and the values; the global RNG is not used.

outdir

Directory for the generated files, default getOption("dMod2.outdir"), else the working directory.

Value

A parfn, called as p(pars, ...), see section Calling a dMod function.

Details

Conserved quantities of an eqnlist enter as \(C x = T\). States without influx are 0. A state whose reactions all vanish with them rests: it takes the value from pars, 0 where pars has none, and is not among the parameters. The root is solved from the states in pars, missing ones at 1, then from all states at 1, then from nStarts random starts; with flow = TRUE the stable root the flow leads to. If all fail, it is an error. A root depends on the parameters, the states in pars and the controls only, not on the calls before it. Identical values are solved once, also across conditions, and conditions are solved in parallel with the cores of the evaluation. keepRoot and controlsPTC can be changed with controls().

Calling a dMod function

The leading arguments depend on the class and are matched by position or by name:

  • prediction function: x(times, pars, ...), returning a prdlist;

  • observation function: g(out, pars, ...) with a prdlist out, returning a prdlist;

  • parameter transformation: p(pars, ...), returning a list with one parvec per condition;

  • objective function: obj(pars, ...), returning an objlist.

pars is a named numeric vector. If it has a deriv attribute, as the output of a parameter transformation does, the derivatives are taken with respect to the parameters behind it. A composition is called according to the resulting class: g * x * p is a prediction function, (g * x * p)(times, pars).

The other arguments are named:

  • fixed: named numeric vector of parameters that enter the evaluation without derivatives. Default NULL.

  • deriv: TRUE (default) returns first derivatives with respect to pars.

  • deriv2: TRUE returns second derivatives as well. Default FALSE. Every function of the chain has to be built for them, see the arguments deriv2 and derivMode of odemodel(), Y() and P().

  • hessian: objective functions only, see the table below. Default NULL.

  • sweep: objective functions only. "forward" (default) propagates the sensitivities through the chain; "reverse" computes the gradient in one backward pass, whose cost does not grow with the number of parameters. "reverse" needs every function of the chain built with derivMode = "reverse", and with "forward-reverse" for deriv2 = TRUE.

  • conditions: character vector, the conditions to evaluate. Default all conditions of the function.

  • env: environment for intermediate results. Default NULL, a new one. An objective function stores the prediction there as prediction and returns the environment as attribute env.

  • cores: number of threads for the ODE solves and the residual kernel. Default getOption("dMod2.cores", 1L).

Prediction, observation and parameter functions accept hessian and sweep and ignore them. With deriv = TRUE an objective function returns this Hessian:

sweephessianderiv2 = FALSEderiv2 = TRUE
"forward"NULL, TRUEGauss-Newtonexact
"forward"FALSEnonenone, with a warning
"reverse"NULLnoneexact
"reverse"TRUEnone, with a warningexact
"reverse"FALSEnonenone, with a warning

hessian = "sparse" returns the Gauss-Newton Hessian of the forward sweep as a sparse Matrix, assembled from the blocks of the conditions; trust() factorizes it where the argument sparse takes the sparse path, and vcov() solves it for the columns of which.

With deriv = FALSE it returns the value alone.

See also

Pexpl(), P(); the guide chapter Setting up models.

Examples

# \donttest{
## Steady state of A <-> B; the total of A and B enters as a parameter
r <- addReaction(NULL, "A", "B", "k1*A")
r <- addReaction(r, "B", "A", "k2*B")
p <- Pimpl(r, condition = "C1", compile = TRUE,
           modelname = "Pimpl_example", outdir = tempdir())
#> using C++ compiler: g++ [-O2 -DNDEBUG -w -fPIC -fopenmp]
#> using C++ compiler: g++ [-O2 -DNDEBUG -w -fPIC -fopenmp]
getParameters(p)
#> [1] "k1"      "k2"      "total_1"
pars <- setNames(c(1, 0.5, 3), getParameters(p))
out <- p(pars)
out$C1
#> Parameter vector:
#>         A :       1
#>         B :       2
#>        k1 :       1
#>        k2 :     0.5
#>   total_1 :       3
#> 
#> Attributes:
#>   deriv  : 5 x 3 matrix
#>   deriv2 : <none>
#>   fixed  : <none>
attr(out$C1, "deriv")
#>                 k1        k2   total_1
#> A       -0.6666667  1.333333 0.3333333
#> B        0.6666667 -1.333333 0.6666667
#> k1       1.0000000  0.000000 0.0000000
#> k2       0.0000000  1.000000 0.0000000
#> total_1  0.0000000  0.000000 1.0000000
# }
